summary: PRIMARY_PRIOR_SUPPORTS_ONE_CARRY_FACTOR_DEFINITION_AUDIT. Both exact full primary papers were independently accessible and bound to their frozen identities. Together they support a narrow prior that crypto carry reflects leveraged demand, market segmentation and constrained arbitrage capital, while also showing that fixed-maturity basis, perpetual funding, liquidation risk and executable arbitrage returns are not interchangeable with BTC spot-return prediction. The permitted mechanism is therefore limited to CRYPTO_CARRY_CONDITIONED_DRA_ENTRY_RISK_VETO: one possible parameter-free pre-entry participation veto on the unchanged unlevered BTC spot DRA. This is causally distinct from derivative execution, carry harvesting, the archived funding-low component, short-build scoring, two-leg funding arbitrage, CFTC positioning, microstructure order flow, post-shock direction, volatility management and the closed rotation, route-substitution and range branches. The conclusion authorizes only one separately frozen pre-outcome factor-definition audit. No source, endpoint, instrument, maturity, formula, threshold, lookback, cadence, side, exit, stop, route or DRA parameter was selected. Existing source plumbing remains OFFLINE_DISABLED_NOT_REGISTERED and installation remains DEFER_CARRY_INSTALL_PRESERVE_R2. Immediate PnL and drawdown effects are ZERO; predictive and economic value remain MISSING_PROOF.

checks.name: POSITIVE_PRIMARY_EVIDENCE
checks.evidence: The BIS paper provides causal and descriptive support that fixed-maturity crypto carry is shaped by smaller trend-following investors seeking leveraged exposure and by constrained arbitrage capital arising from regulatory, balance-sheet and margin frictions. Its micro-futures and spot-ETF natural experiments support demand and segmentation mechanisms. The arXiv paper independently shows that perpetual futures-spot deviations reflect relative futures demand, funding mechanics, trading-cost bounds, past-return momentum and a market-wide common component. Together these support carry as a distinct derivative-market state worthy of one bounded definition audit.

checks.name: FALSIFICATION_PRIMARY_EVIDENCE
checks.evidence: The BIS paper shows severe futures-leg drawdowns, lack of cross-margining and forced short-futures liquidation risk; its cash-and-carry return requires separate spot and futures legs and fixed-date convergence. The arXiv paper states that perpetuals have no guaranteed spot convergence, frames profits as random-maturity arbitrage, requires trading-cost bounds, documents diminishing deviations as markets mature and leaves the causal relation between momentum and perpetual-market pressure open. High arbitrage Sharpe, comovement and historical momentum association therefore do not establish BTC spot-DRA prediction.

checks.name: BASIS_FUNDING_PREDICTION_ARBITRAGE_BOUNDARY
checks.evidence: Fixed-maturity basis is tied to an expiry and convergence; perpetual funding is a recurring transfer without guaranteed expiry convergence. Carry-trade return requires derivative and hedge execution, while the permitted DRA label allows neither. Liquidation prediction concerns short futures positions and cannot be presented as a forecast of spot-DRA returns. No arbitrage return, funding payment or futures-spread statistic was converted into spot alpha.

checks.name: SINGLE_BTC_SPOT_DRA_TRANSFER_BOUNDARY

The DRA source, long-only spot execution, arm, cooldown, one-lot limit, entry confirmation and profit-only exit remain unchanged. The papers do not establish that the veto improves spot returns, PnL or drawdown.
